title: Question Builder — design lock before build
intro:
## What this is

You want a **question builder/composer** for dsh-rich-questions: instead of the model generating one giant `ask_survey` spec in a single tool call (20–40 KB of JSON in practice — slow on every model, truncation-prone on local 27B-class ones, and all research must finish before a word is written), it should **lock a skeleton first** (question ids + branch structure), then **flesh it out in many small patch actions while doing deep research** (codebase, docs, web, 9–12 competitor sweep, all layers of the stack), and finally **launch the wizard** from the assembled tree.

## What your answers decide

Tool surface, skeleton depth, lock strictness, patch rhythm, research storage/enforcement, launch gate, persistence, GUI work, and the v1 fence line. Each answer becomes an implementation rule with tests.

## How long

14 questions, ~6–10 minutes. One question (`q2file`) replaces another depending on your first answer; one (`q5b`) appears only if you pick a grounding bar.

## Grounding facts used below

- The plugin registers exactly **one tool** today (`ask_survey`, ~3.7 KB description alone); engine enforces min-5 options per question, 150-question cap, 1500-char insights.
- The newest commits added **banked answers** (user answers commit early, host-authoritative, survive browser refresh) and crash containment — the same durability posture a draft store would use.
- `src/client.bundle.js` is a 63 KB hand-synced bundle — client work is the most expensive kind this plugin does.

options.description: survey_draft_begin / _patch / _check / _launch as separate globally-registered tools; every call stays a few KB.
options.diagram:
flowchart LR
  begin --> patch
  patch --> research((model research
grep/web/docs))
  research --> patch
  patch --> check
  check --> launch
  launch --> wizard[[user wizard]]
options.insight: What great looks like: every call is small enough for a local 27B to land on the first try, and the host owns the state so a crash mid-build loses nothing — the same posture banked answers just gave the wizard. Tradeoff: four tool schemas to document and the announcement section grows. (Today) the plugin registers exactly one tool via ctx.tools.register; adding more is cheap. Handle: all four tools share one draft registry and one persistence directory.
options.label: Four lifecycle tools

options.description: A single survey_draft tool whose first field is action: begin | patch | check | launch.
options.insight: What great looks like: one name to remember, one announcement line. Tradeoff: one mega-schema whose fields flip meaning per action — weak models leak begin-fields into patch calls, and the schema rivals ask_survey's already-huge description (~3.7 KB). (Today) the largest schema in the plugin is ask_survey itself. Handle: per-action required fields documented inside the schema, not in prose.
options.label: One tool, action param

options.description: The model writes/edits a draft JSON file with its existing write/edit tools; one new tool reads the file and launches.
options.insight: What great looks like: zero new plugin state, drafts are diffable and git-visible, and the model uses file tools it already has — edits can be one-line surgical changes. Tradeoff: no validation until launch — cycles and dangling branch references (the #1 rejection cause today) surface only at the end, the exact late-failure mode we just spent a commit fixing. (Today) the plugin validates whole specs only. Handle: the launch tool returns precise per-error pointers with nearest-id hints, exactly like validateSpec.
options.label: Draft file + launch tool

options.description: Add optional draftId/phase fields to the existing tool instead of new names.
options.insight: What great looks like: nothing new registered, one surface. Tradeoff: overloads a schema that is already the plugin's largest — makes the weak-model problem worse, not better, since every call carries lifecycle fields it usually ignores. (Today) ask_survey's description alone is ~3.7 KB. Handle: only defensible if you want zero new tool names at any cost.
options.label: Extend ask_survey

options.description: No new code; doctrine tells the model to draft in a workspace file, research, then call ask_survey with the finished spec.
options.insight: What great looks like: ships today as a README section. Tradeoff: zero enforcement and the final call is still one giant payload — the slowness and truncation you are reporting stay fully intact. (Today) this is the status quo. Handle: none; it is the do-nothing baseline every other option should beat.
options.label: Prompt-only convention

q1.prompt: How should the model drive the draft? Today one ask_survey call must carry the entire spec in a single generated burst: slow on every model, truncation-prone on small local ones (the exact loop we just patched), and all research must finish before a word is written. The builder splits this into a lifecycle — lock a skeleton, flesh it out in small patches while researching, then launch the wizard. What surface should those lifecycle actions have?

options.description: Per question: id, header, working prompt, multiSelect flag, options with key + working label + branch next; title/intro stubs. Insights, descriptions, sources come later.
options.insight: What great looks like: the whole graph is validated at begin — cycles, dangling next refs, and under-5-option questions die before any research time is spent. Tradeoff: option stances are chosen before evidence exists, so research may force relabeling. (Today) validateSpec already checks all of this; begin would run it in skeleton mode with stub prompts allowed. Handle: begin returns a per-question build checklist in the same response.
options.label: Full frame

options.description: Question ids and branch wiring only; options and prompts arrive during the build.
options.insight: What great looks like: the lightest lock with maximal research freedom. Tradeoff: the min-5-options law and stance quality are invisible until late — a question that research proves needs 7 options may also need a different branch shape, so late structure churn goes up. (Today) nothing validates a bare id map. Handle: check() nags per question until its options land.
options.label: Ids + edges only

options.description: Everything in 'Full frame' plus the up-to-6 quick templates as key+label stubs.
options.insight: What great looks like: the survey's stances are visible from the start, so questions get written to serve them. Tradeoff: stances locked before questions exist tend to fight the two-way coverage rule the engine now enforces (a template must answer every question its branch reaches — and only those). Handle: stub answers are validated only at launch, never at begin.
options.label: Frame + template stubs

options.description: Headers and question ids only, no edges; wiring declared section by section during the build.
options.insight: What great looks like: closest to how brainstorming actually starts. Tradeoff: the branch graph — the plugin's core value — is the last thing to exist, so the 2–3-real-forks doctrine cannot be checked early. (Today) no partial-graph validation exists. Handle: check() reports graph density per section.
options.label: Topic outline only

options.description: begin locks sections; a second outline step adds questions before the build starts.
options.insight: What great looks like: mirrors how big surveys are actually outlined — sections first, questions second. Tradeoff: one more lifecycle step and one more way to be half-begun; the state machine grows a middle state. (Today) no such state exists. Handle: outline is just begin with a flag that permits later structure patches.
options.label: Two-stage begin

q2.prompt: The skeleton is the structure locked on day one, before prose exists: question ids, branch wiring, and — depending on this answer — more or less of each question's frame. How much must the begin step declare? This decides how much planning happens before research starts: the engine can only validate what exists, so more skeleton means earlier graph checks, but also more rework when evidence disagrees with the plan.

options.description: Visible in the repo, survives via git, one file per survey.
options.insight: What great looks like: drafts become reviewable artifacts — you can diff two build sessions and see how research reshaped the tree. Tradeoff: repo noise and accidental commits of half-built surveys. (Today) .dsh directories are workspace-visible to the session's file tools. Handle: README suggests a .gitignore entry; a status field marks launched drafts.
options.label: Workspace .dsh/survey-drafts/<slug>.json

options.description: Machine-private, never in the repo, survives restarts.
options.insight: What great looks like: clean repos, durable drafts. Tradeoff: invisible to git and to you unless you go looking; stale drafts accumulate. (Today) the plugin owns no files; the update-checker's state file in .dsh is the existing pattern. Handle: the launch tool lists stale drafts older than N days.
options.label: Profile-local ~/.dsh/rich-questions/drafts/

options.description: Exactly one draft per workspace, no slugs.
options.insight: What great looks like: zero ambiguity about which draft is active. Tradeoff: parallel topics in one repo stomp each other; a second survey overwrites the first. (Today) nothing enforces single-ness. Handle: launch/begin refuses while an unfinished draft file exists.
options.label: Single canonical file .dsh/survey-draft.json

options.description: Same locations but .yaml — comments allowed, quotes optional.
options.insight: What great looks like: you can annotate the draft by hand while reviewing. Tradeoff: YAML's foot-guns (indentation, the Norway problem) for a model that otherwise speaks JSON natively, and it breaks the plugin's zero-dependency convention unless parsed by a hand-rolled subset parser. (Today) the plugin parses JSON only. Handle: none clean — this option costs a dependency or a parser.
options.label: YAML for hand-editing

options.description: The launch tool accepts any readable file path.
options.insight: What great looks like: maximum freedom, zero convention overhead. Tradeoff: no convention means no way to find stale drafts and no cleanup story. (Today) nothing tracks paths. Handle: launch records the path in a small manifest file.
options.label: Model picks the path

q2file.prompt: You chose a file-based draft: the model composes the survey as a file with its normal write/edit tools, and a launch step turns it into the wizard. Where should that file live, and in what format? (This question replaces the skeleton-depth question — with a file, the model implicitly decides depth by how it writes. Structure-lock and patch-rhythm questions still follow.)

options.description: Content patches anytime; structural patches (ids, edges, options) allowed but each triggers full graph revalidation and bumps a structure-revision counter.
options.insight: What great looks like: research can reshape the tree without a teardown, and every reshape is re-checked — the draft stays launchable at all times. Tradeoff: 'locked' becomes a soft word, and late reshaping can invalidate already-written insights. (Today) validateSpec runs on whole specs, so revalidation is free. Handle: the revision counter appears in check() output as drift telemetry.
options.label: Soft lock, full revalidation

options.description: Content-only patches after begin; structural change requires discard + re-begin.
options.insight: What great looks like: the strongest planning discipline — structure is a promise, research fills it in. Tradeoff: brutal on 20+ question trees when one discovery demands a new branch; everything already written is hostage to the skeleton. Handle: begin refuses skeletons under 5 questions (too flimsy to lock).
options.label: Hard lock

options.description: Structural patches allowed while the draft is under ~40 questions, frozen after.
options.insight: What great looks like: small trees reshape freely, big trees stabilize on time. Tradeoff: an arbitrary cliff — draft #41 makes the tree suddenly brittle for no reason tied to content. Handle: the cap should be a config field, not a hardcoded constant.
options.label: Soft until N questions

options.description: Every structural patch stores the previous skeleton inside the draft file.
options.insight: What great looks like: full auditability of how research reshaped the tree — you can replay the build. Tradeoff: storage churn and a diff format nobody has asked for yet; draft files grow with history. Handle: keep the last 3 snapshots, ring-buffer style.
options.label: Versioned snapshots

options.description: Structural patches pause for a GUI confirmation before applying.
options.insight: What great looks like: you stay the author of the tree's shape. Tradeoff: every reshape blocks on a human — kills autonomous overnight builds; the pending-survey pause machinery is built for one-shot answers, not confirmations. (Today) no confirmation flow exists. Handle: only viable paired with a GUI presence choice later in this survey.
options.label: Operator confirms structure changes

q3.prompt: Once the skeleton is locked, research will sometimes prove the structure wrong — a missing branch, a fork that should rejoin, a question that splits in two. May the build phase change the locked structure, and under what terms? This decides the rework cost whenever evidence disagrees with the plan.

options.description: Each call fully fleshes exactly one question: final prompt, all option descriptions + insights + sources.
options.insight: What great looks like: the smallest reliable unit — a local 27B lands these on the first try, which is the whole point of the builder. Tradeoff: a 30-question survey is 30 calls, and cross-question prose consistency (terminology, anchors) is harder to keep. Handle: check() reports repeated-but-undefined terms as drift hints.
options.label: One question per patch

options.description: Patches follow the header groups; a call carries one section or up to 3 questions.
options.insight: What great looks like: matches how surveys are actually written — a section at a time, its options sharing vocabulary — while calls stay around 4–6 KB, safely under truncation territory. Tradeoff: slightly bigger failure surface per call than one-question patches. Handle: patch refuses more than 3 questions with a clear message.
options.label: One section / 1–3 questions per patch

options.description: Any size patch; check() reports per-question byte budgets.
options.insight: What great looks like: fastest path for big frontier models that never truncate. Tradeoff: reintroduces the giant-payload failure mode on exactly the small models that need the builder. Handle: a soft warning fires over ~8 KB per call.
options.label: Free size, budget-tracked

options.description: Patches are tiny ops: set prompt / add option / attach insight to option X.
options.insight: What great looks like: surgical — reworking one insight never resends its whole question. Tradeoff: 5+ ops per question means 150+ calls for a 30-question survey; op-churn drowns the model's attention. Handle: op batching, which is the next option.
options.label: Field-level ops

options.description: One call submits an array of field-level ops; the host applies them sequentially and stops at the first invalid op, reporting its index.
options.insight: What great looks like: field-level precision with section-level economy — one call can carry 'finalize section 2' as 20 tiny ops, still validated stepwise. Tradeoff: the op array itself can grow big, and stop-at-first-error needs careful messages so the model knows what applied. Handle: cap ops per call (~40) and report applied-count on failure.
options.label: Ordered op-lists

q4.prompt: During the build, the model fleshes out the draft in patch calls (or file edits). How big may one patch be? Smaller calls generate more reliably — especially on local models — but cost more round trips. This sets the rhythm of the entire build phase.

options.description: Judgment options carry sources[] (the field already exists in the schema); check() lists judgment options with zero sources.
options.insight: What great looks like: every hover-insight can show where it came from — the reader-first doctrine's evidence bar, made checkable. Tradeoff: none structural — the field exists and is currently optional with nothing reporting gaps. (Today) sources are decorative. Handle: one line per question in check() output.
options.label: Sources on options, gaps reported

options.description: Launch refuses when any judgment option's insight lacks evidence — strictness set in the next question.
options.insight: What great looks like: turns 'research-grounded' from aspiration into a gate; the failure moves from silent (vague insights) to blocking (launch error listing each ungrounded option). Tradeoff: a hard gate can block launch on a model that researched badly rather than vaguely — blocking failures need clear remediation text. Handle: the launch error lists every ungrounded option with its question.
options.label: Grounding bar at launch

options.description: A free-text evidence field stored per question while building — quotes, numbers, file paths — stripped at launch.
options.insight: What great looks like: the model's research scratchpad lives with the question it feeds, so evidence survives across turns instead of scrolling out of context. Tradeoff: draft files grow, and stripping must be tested so notes never leak into the wizard. (Today) no such field exists. Handle: a reserved field name the launch step always drops.
options.label: Research notes per question

options.description: Research notes also render in the question's detail area for the user.
options.insight: What great looks like: the user sees the receipts behind each question while answering. Tradeoff: couples draft internals to the 63 KB hand-synced client bundle — real client work, the most expensive kind here. (Today) the bundle renders only pending surveys. Handle: ride the existing detail field; no new UI.
options.label: Evidence rendered in the wizard

options.description: Research artifacts live only in the conversation; the draft stores final copy.
options.insight: What great looks like: zero new schema, zero new rules. Tradeoff: nothing checkable — the grounding story degrades to trust-me, and long builds lose early research to context scroll. Handle: none.
options.label: Nothing stored

q5.prompt: The research itself — codebase greps, web searches, the 9–12 competitor sweep, docs — stays in the model's hands; the plugin only owns structured state. What should the draft store and enforce around research? Pick every behavior you want; each selection becomes a tested rule.

options.description: Any credible link or citation counts.
options.insight: What great looks like: the cheapest bar that still forces a research pass before launch. Tradeoff: one link can be decorative — a single URL does not mean the claim came from it. Handle: source strings must be non-empty and pairwise distinct per option.
options.label: ≥1 source per judgment insight

options.description: Each judgment insight cites ≥1 source, and each question carries ≥1 option naming a concrete comparison target (a competitor, product, or file).
options.insight: What great looks like: bakes the 9–12 competitor sweep into validation — 'compares to X' becomes a checkable unit, the Push doctrine made structural. Tradeoff: the hardest bar; surveys on internal topics with no competitors need an escape hatch. Handle: a begin flag like grounding: internal skips only the comparison half.
options.label: Source + named comparison per question

options.description: Only recommended (badged) options must be grounded; others are advisory.
options.insight: What great looks like: enforcement lands where eyes go first. Tradeoff: the non-recommended options — exactly the ones a skeptic picks — go ungrounded. Handle: check() still reports all gaps softly.
options.label: Grounded recommendations only

options.description: check() reports a grounding percentage; launch never blocks on it.
options.insight: What great looks like: informative, never blocking. Tradeoff: a bar that cannot refuse is a suggestion — under deadline pressure models will ship at 40% grounded. Handle: the percentage appears in every check() output so drift is visible.
options.label: Soft score, no gate

options.description: begin sets groundingBar: off | soft | strict, default strict.
options.insight: What great looks like: the right strictness per survey type — internal retro vs competitive positioning. Tradeoff: the model picks its own enforcement, and under pressure everything becomes 'off'. Handle: default strict; the flag's value is echoed in every check() output.
options.label: Per-draft strictness flag

q5b.prompt: You picked a grounding bar: launch refuses when insights lack evidence. How strict is 'grounded'? This is the rule the model must satisfy after its research sweep, so it decides how much citation work every built survey costs.

options.description: The same rules ask_survey enforces today: graph integrity, min-5 options, size caps.
options.insight: What great looks like: zero new law — anything ask_survey accepts, the builder launches. Tradeoff: stub prompts and placeholder labels pass; a 'finished' survey can read like scaffolding to the user. (Today) this is the whole rulebook. Handle: none — this is the baseline the other options extend.
options.label: Current validateSpec, nothing more

options.description: Additionally every question prompt and option label must be non-stub — begin writes explicit stub markers, so 'working title' is detectable.
options.insight: What great looks like: the user never sees scaffolding language in a launched wizard; 'done' means done. Tradeoff: one more rule to satisfy — but check() lists the stubs mechanically, so it is cheap to obey. (Today) no stub concept exists; begin would introduce it. Handle: a stub is any string starting with 'TODO:' — greppable, self-documenting, trivially tested.
options.label: validateSpec + completeness

options.description: The strictest union: your grounding-bar choice enforced on top of completeness.
options.insight: What great looks like: launch means fully valid, fully written, fully grounded — the reader-first doctrine enforced end to end. Tradeoff: the longest builds; a missing citation now blocks the wizard. Handle: the launch error groups failures by kind (structure / stubs / grounding) so the model fixes in one pass.
options.label: validateSpec + completeness + grounding

options.description: Launch always starts the wizard and attaches a completion report.
options.insight: What great looks like: never blocks a demo or a time-boxed session. Tradeoff: the wizard is user-facing — warnings that arrive after launch are hindsight, and the user is already answering questions built on gaps. Handle: the report is also returned to the model.
options.label: Warn and proceed

options.description: Launch enters a preview state; a second confirm (tool call or GUI button) starts the wizard.
options.insight: What great looks like: a dry-run moment for big surveys — you glance before the user is interrupted. Tradeoff: a double step on every survey, even 5-question ones, in a tool already built around pausing. Handle: preview only above ~15 questions.
options.label: Preview step before wizard

q6.prompt: survey_draft_launch turns the finished draft into the live wizard. What must be true before it will start? This is the builder's definition of done.

options.description: ~/.dsh/rich-questions/drafts/<draftId>.json — survives restarts, machine-private, kept after launch with status: launched.
options.insight: What great looks like: a crash mid-build loses nothing — reopen by id and continue, the same recovery posture banked answers just gave the wizard. Tradeoff: invisible to git; stale drafts accumulate silently. (Today) the plugin owns no files; the dsh-update-checker's state file in .dsh is the existing local-state pattern. Handle: check() lists drafts older than N days as stale.
options.label: Profile-local JSON, one file per draft

options.description: Drafts live in the host process; a restart loses them.
options.insight: What great looks like: simplest implementation — one Map, no file I/O, no cleanup. Tradeoff: a build spanning a restart (update, crash, machine sleep) evaporates — and long multi-turn builds are the entire point of this feature. Handle: none; the weakness is inherent.
options.label: Session memory only

options.description: Drafts are repo files, git-visible and cross-machine via clone.
options.insight: What great looks like: durable, reviewable, shareable — the build travels with the repo. Tradeoff: repo noise, merge conflicts on synced trees, half-built surveys riding along in commits. Handle: a suggested .gitignore line plus a README note.
options.label: Workspace .dsh/survey-drafts/

options.description: Canonical file in the profile, plus a regenerated mirror copy in the workspace when one exists.
options.insight: What great looks like: durability and visibility at once. Tradeoff: two copies to keep coherent — mirror drift becomes a new failure mode. Handle: the mirror is strictly write-only (regenerated after every patch, never read).
options.label: Profile file + workspace mirror

options.description: Canonical in the profile; a survey_draft_export call dumps it to any path on request.
options.insight: What great looks like: visibility only when wanted — no standing noise, no drift. Tradeoff: one more lifecycle action to document and get wrong. Handle: export takes a path and refuses to overwrite existing files.
options.label: Profile file + explicit export tool

q7.prompt: Where does draft state live, and what survives a harness restart or a crashed session? (The pending-survey registry already survives browser refreshes; this is about the build phase, which can span many turns and even model sessions.)

options.description: Drafts are model-side; the chat shows ordinary tool-call lines; only the finished wizard renders.
options.insight: What great looks like: the whole feature ships with zero client-bundle changes — smallest diff, no sync burden, fastest review. Tradeoff: during a long build you watch tool calls scroll, not progress. (Today) the bundle renders only pending surveys. Handle: check() emits a compact progress summary the model can relay in text.
options.label: Invisible in v1

options.description: A small card — draft title, X/Y questions fleshed, grounding % — pushed over the existing SSE stream.
options.insight: What great looks like: live visibility at modest cost — one new SSE event type plus one card built from existing primitives. Tradeoff: bundle work (the 63 KB hand-synced file) and a new event shape to keep stable across versions. Handle: the event carries only counts, never draft content.
options.label: Progress card in chat

options.description: A tree view with per-question states, research notes, grounding indicators.
options.insight: What great looks like: the power view — you audit the build, not just the result. Tradeoff: the largest client surface the plugin would ever have had — effectively a second wizard; a v1 scope explosion. Handle: defer behind a manual route in v2.
options.label: Full draft explorer

options.description: No client work; the model narrates progress between patches.
options.insight: What great looks like: free, and often enough — the model is already in the loop and can say 'section 2 of 4 done, 3 gaps left'. Tradeoff: reports depend on the model remembering to relay them. Handle: check() output is pre-formatted for easy quoting.
options.label: Model-relayed only

options.description: A server-rendered HTML status page you open yourself; no chat integration.
options.insight: What great looks like: full detail on demand with zero bundle changes. Tradeoff: nothing in the app points you at it — a URL you must remember exists. Handle: server-rendered table inside the existing loopback-fenced routes.
options.label: Manual status page

q8.prompt: Should you see the draft while it is being built, or does only the finished wizard render? Client work is the most expensive kind this plugin does — the browser bundle is a 63 KB hand-synced file.

options.description: check() nags for templates once every question is fleshed; stances are chosen over finished content.
options.insight: What great looks like: templates that actually fit the tree — the two-way coverage rule (a template answers every question its branch reaches, and only those) is easiest to satisfy when the tree is final. Tradeoff: one more phase at the end of every build. (Today) templates ride in the one-shot spec and are a top rejection cause. Handle: check() proposes each template's reachable path as a hint.
options.label: After questions complete

options.description: Keys + labels early, answers filled at the end.
options.insight: What great looks like: the stances frame the build from day one. Tradeoff: early stances fight late question edits — the coverage rule punishes drift, so stubs get rewritten anyway. Handle: stub answers validated only at launch.
options.label: Stubbed at begin

options.description: A begin flag wantsQuick; drafts without it never get templates.
options.insight: What great looks like: right-sized — small or internal surveys skip the ceremony entirely. Tradeoff: one more begin flag to document and default correctly. Handle: default true (the doctrine wants templates).
options.label: Optional per draft

options.description: check() drafts template skeletons from the recommended options; the model edits them.
options.insight: What great looks like: a cheap starting point for the least creative part of authoring. Tradeoff: auto-stances tend toward incoherent bundles — five 'recommended' picks do not make a philosophy, and the coverage rule rejects half-built ones. Handle: proposals are clearly marked non-authoritative and never auto-applied.
options.label: Host-proposed

options.description: Builder drafts carry no templates; they would be added by a later edit.
options.insight: What great looks like: minimal build, minimal rules. Tradeoff: the wizard loses its one-click path — and for a big researched survey, that is exactly where templates pay off most. Handle: none.
options.label: Never

q9.prompt: The up-to-6 quick templates (one-click whole-survey answer stances, keys a–f) are part of the final spec. When are they authored during the build? (The engine now enforces a two-way rule: a template must answer every question its branch reaches, and only those.)

options.description: Create the pending survey in the existing registry, render the wizard in the composer seat, block until the user answers or picks reroll/push/discuss; the draft is marked launched.
options.insight: What great looks like: zero new interaction semantics — the wizard, SSE, refresh recovery, and preflight buttons all just work, battle-tested. Tradeoff: launch blocks mid-turn exactly like ask_survey does today. (Today) service.ask() and the preflight outcomes already exist. Handle: launch delegates to the same service.ask().
options.label: Exactly what ask_survey does

options.description: Launch enters a preview state; a confirm step (second call or GUI button) starts the wizard.
options.insight: What great looks like: a dry-run gate for big surveys. Tradeoff: a double step on every survey, even tiny ones. Handle: preview only above ~15 questions.
options.label: Preview gate first

options.description: Launch returns the assembled spec; the model calls ask_survey itself.
options.insight: What great looks like: builder and wizard stay decoupled — each tool does one job. Tradeoff: the final ask_survey call is again one giant single payload — the exact failure mode this feature exists to kill. Handle: none; the weakness is inherent to the handoff.
options.label: Hand back the spec

options.description: Everything in the first option, plus: when the user hits Reroll, the launched draft reopens as an editable draft instead of forcing a from-scratch rebuild.
options.insight: What great looks like: reroll becomes cheap — edit three questions, relaunch; the research investment survives the user's first reaction. Tradeoff: the draft lifecycle grows a 'reopened' state. (Today) reroll discards everything and the model rebuilds blind. Handle: launched drafts are kept (status: launched) precisely for this.
options.label: Launch + reopen-on-reroll

options.description: Launch returns immediately with the surveyId; the wizard appears when the model's turn ends.
options.insight: What great looks like: the model can finish narrating before the user is interrupted — nicer conversational flow. Tradeoff: diverges from ask_survey's block-until-answered contract; two tools, two timing semantics to document. (Today) the pending registry already supports late rendering. Handle: document the difference in both tools.
options.label: Deferred start

q10.prompt: What does launching actually do, moment to moment? This decides how the builder hands off to the wizard you already use.

options.description: begin creates or switches the active draft; patch/check/launch address the active one implicitly; ids exist for reopening.
options.insight: What great looks like: parallel topics without id-juggling in every call — the common path stays terse. Tradeoff: implicit state can surprise — a patch lands in the wrong draft after a forgotten begin. Handle: every tool response names the draft it touched.
options.label: Many drafts, one active per session

options.description: begin refuses while an unfinished draft exists — launch or discard first.
options.insight: What great looks like: the strongest hygiene — no zombie drafts, ever. Tradeoff: topic switching forces discards, and a crashed build blocks all new surveys until cleaned. Handle: discard is one call.
options.label: Exactly one unfinished draft

options.description: Every patch/check/launch carries draftId; no implicit active draft.
options.insight: What great looks like: zero ambiguity about which draft a call touches. Tradeoff: every call grows an id field, and weak models will typo ids — friction the active-draft pattern exists to avoid. Handle: the id is echoed in every result for correlation.
options.label: Many, always explicit

options.description: Many drafts, each carrying a human title that lists and errors display.
options.insight: What great looks like: friendliest errors — 'patch rejected in: API deprecation survey'. Tradeoff: titles are another stub field that must be kept non-stub. Handle: title required at begin and completeness-checked like prompts.
options.label: Many + human titles

options.description: Drafts are scoped to the chat thread, shared across agents in it.
options.insight: What great looks like: matches how threads feel; a delegated researcher subagent could contribute patches to the same draft — genuinely useful. Tradeoff: the host has session ids, not conversation ids — a new scoping concept with murky subagent boundaries. (Today) pending surveys are keyed by session id. Handle: scope by session root agent.
options.label: One per conversation

q11.prompt: How many drafts can be alive at once, and how are they addressed? This decides the state model every tool call carries.

options.description: v1 touches only host, engine, and tools; the browser side is untouched.
options.insight: What great looks like: the diff stays reviewable and the 63 KB hand-synced bundle is not touched at all; pairs with an invisible or model-relayed GUI choice. Tradeoff: no progress UI in v1. (Today) the bundle inlines the engine verbatim — every client change doubles the sync surface. Handle: a README line promising the fence.
options.label: No client-bundle changes

options.description: The plugin never calls web_search/grep/read itself — it stores and checks citations only.
options.insight: What great looks like: the plugin stays zero-dependency and single-purpose; research remains the model's job with its own tools. Tradeoff: the plugin cannot verify a source is real — only that one is present. Handle: none needed beyond wording.
options.label: No research execution

options.description: Drafts are machine-local; no export/import protocol in v1.
options.insight: What great looks like: one less consistency problem; the state model stays a single local file. Tradeoff: a build started at the desk cannot continue from the laptop. Handle: an export tool can arrive later without migration.
options.label: No cross-machine sync

options.description: Soft-lock revalidation bumps a counter; no snapshot diffs in v1.
options.insight: What great looks like: draft state stays one small file with a number for drift telemetry. Tradeoff: no archaeology on how research reshaped the tree. Handle: the counter alone, surfaced in check().
options.label: No version history beyond a counter

options.description: check() never drafts template skeletons; the model writes its own stances.
options.insight: What great looks like: avoids shipping half-coherent auto-stance bundles the coverage rule would reject anyway. Tradeoff: more authoring work per survey. Handle: check() lists reachability hints instead of proposals.
options.label: No auto-proposed templates

q12.prompt: Last one — the v1 fence line. Pick everything that must stay OUT of the first build so it ships small and reviewable. Each picked fence becomes a promise with a README line.

quick.description: Four small tools, full-frame skeleton, soft lock, section-sized patches, sources + research notes, completeness gate, profile-local files, zero GUI work.
quick.insight: The posture that maximizes reliability for small models and reviewability for you: every call stays a few KB, the host owns durable state (crash mid-build loses nothing), the graph is validated from minute one, and the whole feature ships without touching the 63 KB client bundle. Grounding is reported but not gated — research discipline without a blocking bar in v1.
quick.label: Host-authoritative lifecycle (Recommended)

quick.description: Draft as a workspace JSON file edited with existing file tools; one launch tool reads it; no new plugin state.
quick.insight: The smallest possible plugin diff: no registry, no persistence code, no new schemas beyond one launch tool — the model composes with write/edit it already has, and drafts are git-diffable. The cost is late validation (structure errors surface only at launch) and a final handoff that can still be a big call — pick this if you value transparency over enforcement.
quick.label: Minimal file path

quick.description: One tool with actions, versioned snapshots, op-list patches, strict source+comparison grounding, SSE progress card, host-proposed templates, reopen-on-reroll.
quick.insight: The maximal build: research evidence enforced at the bar the Push doctrine already preaches (source + named comparison per question), visible progress in chat, full audit of structure changes, and rerolls that reopen the draft instead of nuking it. Costs the most — client bundle work, the strictest gate, the longest builds.
quick.label: Grounded & visible

quick.description: Ids+edges skeleton, hard structure lock, one question per patch, session-memory state, no templates, plain validateSpec gate.
quick.insight: The most conservative tooling: minimal new law, minimal state, minimal schema — but it keeps one unfinished draft at a time, loses builds on restart (session memory), and skips quick templates entirely. A probe of how little machinery you find acceptable before the feature stops being worth it.
quick.label: Strict and small
